entryAnswer.explanation:
What the code does. `spendingAlertsFor(graph, defaults)` binds one immutable default set and returns a frozen `compose` (causal-entry.ts:48-77). `configuration` freezes `{name, diagnostics}` and defaults diagnostics to "off" (causal-entry.ts:36-46), so the shared defaults are `{name: "alerts-a", diagnostics: "off"}`. Each `compose(inputs, overrides)` re-validates the caller's plain input object, requires a prepared `SpendingResource` (`SpendingResource.is`, causal-entry.ts:54-58), and calls the existing complete host construction `composeSpendingHost(graph, inputs, resource.binding, resource, options)` (causal-entry.ts:59-69). It returns the host plus `view` and `capabilities` (causal-entry.ts:70-74). The two calls therefore produce two independent runtimes in the same Graph, with distinct names `alerts-a`/`alerts-b` and `diagnostics: "summary"` only on the second. `mountSpendingView(view, render)` subscribes the five ports of that exact view and returns a stop function that ends observation only (causal-view-binding.ts:16-56). The returned pair exposes each original instance and its own cleanup.

What the application must retain after either display is unmounted. Detaching a panel stops observation; it does not close the instance or release its obligations (README.md:143, causal-view-binding.ts:16). The application must keep, per instance: (1) the owning Graph and the original composed instance (`app.owner`, `app.inspect`, `app.runEndReady`, `app.guard`, `app.source`) — the demo keeps `app.owner` and `app.inspect` (causal-graded-demo.ts:65, 140-143, 185-188); (2) the original `.view` and the original issued capabilities, including `capabilities.retained` lineage, because frameworks pass the original identity/execution/retained handles and a structural copy is not an issued object (README.md:91-96, causal-audience.examples.ts:17-25); (3) the host's retained request/admission/outcome records, which survive detach and are bounded at 64 per owned epoch with one in-flight write (README.md:146-151, causal-focused-host.ts:140, 368-373, 571-575); (4) the request references needed to correlate the publication projection with those records (README.md:125-132, causal-graded-demo.ts:207-211). A missing publication does not mean no request was submitted, and `runEndReady`/`normalEndReady` are readiness conditions, not proof of termination or resource release (README.md:129-132, 144).

Distinct names. The name is a node-namespace prefix, not an authorization token: `spendingNodeNames` builds `${name}/startup`, `${name}/...`, `${name}/causal/...`, `${name}/publication` and, only for `diagnostics === "summary"`, `${name}/diagnosticSummary` (causal-preset.ts:60-72). Distinct names keep the two instances' nodes and edges distinguishable in one Graph, and the host guard checks `view.authorityId === `${name}/causal/authority`` (causal-focused-host.ts:310-311). Changing a name does not clone input Nodes, create an independent resource or rewrite its binding (README.md:85-89).

Independently prepared input Nodes. `spendingInputNodes` requires four exact groups and six distinct input Nodes (causal-preset.ts:73-93); the host wires `inputs.evaluations.pack/arrivals/current`, `inputs.verification.receipts` and `inputs.localAuthority.facts` as its declared edges (causal-focused-host.ts:88-94). Each input frame is validated against the expected binding (`checkInput`, causal-inputs.ts:352-437), and the host's guard requires the material snapshot's `packRef` to match the binding (causal-focused-host.ts:309-313). Two independently prepared inputs give each instance its own evaluation/verification/authority facts and its own occurrence identity, so one instance's facts cannot be substituted for the other's; the demo prepares separate `sources` and `sourcesB` (causal-graded-demo.ts:46, 95).

Resource bindings. `compose` requires a prepared resource and passes `resource.binding` and the resource itself to the host (causal-entry.ts:55-68). The host validates the binding and requires `same(resource.binding, binding)` (causal-focused-host.ts:74-77), then `resource.claim()` takes the single cold lease for that resource (causal-focused-host.ts:96, causal-resource.ts:69-99). A resource can be claimed once, so two instances need two separately prepared resources with their own bindings (compositionEpoch/hostEpoch/destinationRef); the demo uses `presetBinding` and a second `bindingB` with `compositionEpoch: 2`, `hostEpoch: 2` (causal-graded-demo.ts:89-110). The binding is what ties the instance's material, admission and publication to one destination and epoch; changing a name does not rebind it.

Scope. The snippet only composes and mounts; it does not open resources, invent input facts or call a transport. Normal host behavior (including the simulated writer) is left intact.
